title: SMILE: LLC-based Shared Memory Expansion to Improve GPU Thread Level Parallelism
problem: GPUs suffer from low thread occupancy and limited data throughput due to constrained on-chip resources like shared memory and register file. While last-level caches are enlarged to support growing computation, applications cannot fully utilize the excessive LLC space.
motivation: Improving GPU thread occupancy and data throughput is critical for maximizing performance in memory-bound compute applications.
method: SMILE converts part of the last-level cache into shared memory (memory that GPU threads can simultaneously access) while keeping the rest as a normal data cache. To find the right split for each application, it tries different partition sizes and measures actual performance while the application runs (online profiling). This approach increases the shared memory available to threads, which removes the scheduling bottleneck that currently limits how many threads can run in parallel.
key_novelty: The key idea is expanding shared memory by partitioning the last-level cache, with the partition automatically tuned to each application.
contributions: Software-based LLC partitioning mechanism to dynamically expand shared memory
Adaptive online profiling framework to determine optimal partition grades per application
14.7% average performance improvement over baseline configuration
primary_theme: dynamic LLC partitioning for GPU shared memory expansion
